title: Book
description: A long-form title somebody is writing: what it is about, how far along it is, and where its cover sits. The chapters are not inside it — each is its own record pointing back, so a book can be read without carrying its whole text.

id.description: The record's own id in the system that holds it.

author.description: The wallet, handle, or id under localIds of whoever is writing it. Absent while the title belongs to nobody yet.

session.description: The id of the working session the book was started from, in the system that holds that session. Absent when it was not started from one.

subtitle.description: The line under the title, when there is one.

description.description: What the book is about, in the words of whoever is writing it. Written for a reader deciding, not for a catalogue.

genre.description: The shelf it belongs on. A closed list because it decides how the title is filed, not how it reads.

language.description: The language the book is written in, as a BCP 47 tag such as pt, en or pt-BR.

status.description: How far along it is. Which move from which is a rule held beside the type, never in it.

aiModel.description: The model that helped write it, named as the system that called it names it. Absent when nothing was asked of one.

targetWordCount.description: The length being aimed at, set by whoever is writing. Zero while no target was chosen.

currentWordCount.description: Words written so far across the chapters. Counted by whoever holds the text, carried here so a reader of the book alone can say how far along it is.

coverPrompt.description: The brief the cover image was asked for with. Kept because the image can be asked for again.

cover.description: The cover image, where it is kept. Absent while the title has none.

kdpKeywords.description: The keywords the title is listed under on the store. Free text, in the words of whoever sells it.

kdpBisac.description: The BISAC subject code given to the store, such as FIC000000. Separate from genre: one is ours, this one is the trade's.
